rubrics.criterion: The table-structure view path no longer ships computation that cannot execute: the guarded statistics/advisory statements inside that view are removed (or rewritten so they are reachable from the shipped configuration without changing the rendered page), and the helpers that served only this dormant path -- the dataset-class statistics reader, its memoizing wrapper, the row-footprint estimate, and the module-level advisory formatter -- are removed too, unless an individual helper keeps or gains a genuinely reachable call site.
rubrics.rationale: This is the primary dormant cluster of the instance; it ties the dataset layer, a module-level formatter, and one of the application's table views together, so an incomplete pass that leaves either the branch or any of its helpers in place must be caught.

rubrics.criterion: The export flow no longer ships inactive manifest wiring: the guarded manifest statements inside the export view are removed (or reintegrated as genuinely reachable code that preserves the pinned export behavior), and the module-level manifest formatter plus any helper reachable only through it is removed as well, unless it retains a live caller elsewhere.
rubrics.rationale: The export cluster is the second large dormant feature path; its helper is also the sole link keeping the executor's query-cost estimator dormant, so a partial removal here leaves a chain of unreachable definitions behind.

rubrics.criterion: In the statement-execution module, the statements written after the error-path terminating statement in the multi-statement loop are removed, and the result-key encoder helper that those statements were the only caller of is deleted -- or, if retained, is wired to code that can actually execute.
rubrics.rationale: This cluster tests the solver on the subtler deadness form the instance mixes in: statements unreachable by position rather than by guard, whose helper would otherwise look like a normal utility of the module.

rubrics.criterion: The standalone gevent server script contains no dormant pool-sizing path: the gated branch in its bootstrap and the pool-sizing helper it was the only caller of are removed, so the bootstrap constructs its worker pool through exactly one, reachable code path.
rubrics.rationale: The server entry script is a separate execution path from the request-handling application; this rubric ensures the removal spanned that component instead of stopping at the Flask module.

rubrics.criterion: The solution does not attempt to resolve the dormant paths by enabling them: no module-level switch, protocol level, or dialect constant is raised or toggled to make the never-executing code run, and the shipped defaults are byte-identical to the pinned build apart from the removal of dormant wiring.
rubrics.rationale: Flipping the dormant switches is the tempting one-edit fix this instance is built to punish: it would newly execute statistics queries against ordinary databases and visibly change behavior, which fails both the behavior boundary and the task's goal of removing un-executed code.

rubrics.criterion: Import lists stay consistent with the surviving definitions: no import names a helper that was deleted, and the import entries that existed only to reference removed scaffolding -- in particular the application module's import of an executor helper that had no possible active caller -- are pruned or repointed.
rubrics.rationale: The instance deliberately plants a wiring illusion in an import list; a solver who deletes helper definitions but leaves the import lines has left orphaned references behind, which this case's verification explicitly asks to avoid.

rubrics.criterion: Live utilities that dormant code merely referenced are not collateral damage: the row-key encode/decode helpers behind the detail-row links, statement splitting, single-query execution, and the dataset class's cached accessors that the table templates render all remain present and functional.
rubrics.rationale: The dormant clusters deliberately sit adjacent to heavily used machinery (the result-key encoder sits beside the real row-key coder); a plausible over-deletion failure mode for this instance is deleting live utilities along with the dead ones, and the test suite directly imports several of them.

rubrics.criterion: No module-level configuration constant survives as scaffolding-only residue: the protocol, dialect, and toggle constants whose only consumers were the removed dormant paths are themselves removed, unless some surviving live code still reads them.
rubrics.rationale: Switches that gate nothing are the last artifact the dormant features left behind; they are not reported by statement-level reachability alone, so this rubric grades the cleanup step that a minimal patch would skip.

rubrics.criterion: No comment or inline protocol note survives that describes only the removed dormant paths (e.g. notes explaining what a switch level enables are removed together with the switch and its branch).
rubrics.rationale: Threaded commentary was part of making the dormant work look landed; leaving it behind after removing the code leaves the module describing behavior it no longer contains.

rubrics.criterion: Rendering a table's structure page does not newly read planner statistics: for a database that has never had statistics collected, the structure page still renders successfully with the same payload as the pinned build (no 500, no new warning path), and the app never performs a per-table statistics query during a structure request.
rubrics.rationale: The single most likely regression in this instance is activating or half-activating the dormant statistics branch: it queries a maintenance table ordinary databases lack and would break the structure page at request time.

rubrics.criterion: Export behavior is untouched by the removal: for every export format the response body, status code, and header set are identical to the pinned build, with no manifest-style header appearing unconditionally or conditionally where the pinned build produced none.
rubrics.rationale: The dormant export statements write to the response itself, so an incomplete or over-eager repair could change what every export download looks like; nothing in the visible export behavior may drift.

rubrics.criterion: The multi-statement runner behaves exactly as the pinned build on scripts that fail partway: it stops at the first failing statement and returns exactly the results collected before the failure, with no appended results, no mutated fields on any returned item, and unchanged rendering of successful results including pagination.
rubrics.rationale: The unreachable statements in the loop were written exactly where a careless edit would place live ones -- directly on the failure path -- so this rubric pins the observable failure semantics the repair must not rereoute or enrich.

rubrics.criterion: The standalone server's startup remains equivalent to the pinned build: it constructs the same fixed-size worker pool with the same spawn wiring at the same point of the bootstrap, and imports the same gevent machinery it did before the dormant path was removed.
rubrics.rationale: The server script has no test coverage in this repository, so a repair that reorders or alters its bootstrap would otherwise pass silently; this rubric grades that untested execution path by inspection.
